idiom_name: handler or constructor wrapping: func(C) C, the middleware idiom (typed with generics since Go 1.18)
implementation_notes: In Go a component is a value - usually an http.Handler, a widget constructor or a render function - so the enhancer is an ordinary function that takes one and returns one: the classic func(http.Handler) http.Handler middleware wrapper, or a generic func WithLogging[P any](next Component[P]) Component[P] once type parameters are available (Go's official generics tutorial shows the constraint form). This is the standard middleware idiom rather than a structure to hand-write, and chains are composed by nesting or by a small slice-based helper. The classic wrapper is still justified where the wrapped value must satisfy a framework interface, because the outer type then has to implement that interface - and its optional interfaces - as well.
pitfalls: A wrapper around http.ResponseWriter hides the optional interfaces of the underlying writer (Flusher, Hijacker, Pusher), which breaks streaming, websockets and HTTP/2 push until they are forwarded explicitly.
Closures capture request and loop state: before Go 1.22 a loop variable shared across iterations makes every enhanced component behave as the last iteration's.

Interface satisfaction is structural: a wrapper that does not implement the framework's interface (or its optional parts) still compiles where a concrete type is used and fails only at the assertion or the call site.
